Runs after `tct-page-change` with the new page; the paginator is busy (`aria-busy`, `:state(busy)`) while a returned promise is pending, rapid clicks are not blocked, and the previous page returns if it rejects.

`page-size-options="10, 25, 50"` or a `number[]` property; shows the page-size selector.

The dots are one tab stop; arrows move focus and the page together (selection follows focus), Home and End jump, focus wraps, arrows follow the reading direction.

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `page` and `page-size` are applied by the element when `tct-page-change` and `tct-page-size-change` are not prevented; upstream is controlled (`page` plus `onChange`). Preventing the event, or setting the property back, keeps the paginator controlled.

A request for the page that is already current (clicking the current page button) fires nothing; upstream calls `onChange` with the current page. The page-size change is the exception: it always asks for page 1 so a loader can rely on it.
When both are given `total-items` wins over `total-pages`, as upstream documents; upstream's code lets `totalPages` win, which disagrees with its count readout.

`hasFirstLast` (default true) is the inverted `no-first-last` attribute; `isDisabled` is `disabled`; `page-size-options` also parses from an attribute; `xstyle` and `data-testid` are replaced by class, style, `::part()` and host attributes.

Each dot is a 24px target that paints an 8px disc (WCAG 2.5.8) instead of an 8px button; the current dot is `aria-current="page"` and the only tab stop. The input, page-size selector and buttons keep their own events inside the paginator (`input`, `change`, `tct-enter` do not leave it).
Ghost buttons, the neutral fill of the current page number and the accent dot use the shared Tecton tokens; chevrons mirror in right-to-left through the icon's own direction handling.

core.pagination.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] a real <nav> and buttons in the shadow tree, the dots as one tab stop; [mwg:accessibility] politeness, target size and names. The sixteen upstream messages are all used and tested in de-DE.
